keyVerseText: Unto whom the prince of the eunuchs gave names: for he gave unto Daniel the name of Belteshazzar; and to Hananiah, of Shadrach; and to Mishael, of Meshach; and to Azariah, of Abednego.
rootMeaning: The name בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר (Belteshazzar) is of foreign derivation, likely Babylonian, and is understood to mean 'lord of the straitened's treasure' or related to protection of life or the king. This suggests a title or name conveying authority and guardianship, reflecting a status connected to divine or royal protection. The literal sense enriches our understanding beyond the English transliteration by emphasizing the role of divine sovereignty and stewardship implicit in the name.
usageInScripture: This proper name appears twice in Scripture and is consistently translated as 'Belteshazzar,' the Babylonian name given to Daniel by Nebuchadnezzar. Its usage is tightly focused on identifying Daniel in his Babylonian context, highlighting his role and identity in the foreign empire. This consistency underscores the significance of his Babylonian name as a marker of his captivity and exalted position within the empire.
theologicalSignificance: The original meaning of Belteshazzar as 'lord of the straitened's treasure' or a protector figure underscores Daniel's unique position as a faithful servant of God who is also elevated in a pagan kingdom. It reminds believers that God sovereignly places His servants in positions of influence even in adverse circumstances, preserving and using them for His purposes. Daniel's name reflects both his captivity and God's providential care, pointing to the faithfulness and holiness required to stand firm in a foreign culture. This name and its bearer foreshadow Christ, who is the ultimate protector and sovereign Lord over all earthly powers.
keyVerseReflection: Daniel 1:7 states, 'Unto whom the prince of the eunuchs gave names: for he gave unto Daniel the name of Belteshazzar.' This verse reveals the imposition of a Babylonian identity on Daniel, symbolizing his captivity and the beginning of his service in Babylon. The name Belteshazzar contributes a deeper meaning by signifying Daniel's role under divine protection and authority even in exile, affirming God's sovereign hand over his life and mission.
